# A ```{typst} block looks like an executable cell to Quarto's engine
# detection, which then selects Jupyter and fails for want of a kernel. The
# extension compiles those blocks itself, so the page needs no engine.
engine: markdown
---

Typst draws diagrams, tables, and equations well, and Quarto can render to Typst.
The moment the same document also has to produce HTML, a PDF through LaTeX, or a Word file, none of that Typst is available.

`typst-render` compiles the Typst instead of passing it through.
A `{typst}` block becomes an image, built by the Typst binary Quarto already ships, so the figure survives into every format.

## Installation

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Or install it from your editor with [Quarto Wizard](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard):

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

[Visual Studio Code](vscode://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Visual Studio Code using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[Positron](positron://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in Positron using the Quarto Wizard extension."}
[VSCodium](vscodium://mcanouil.quarto-wizard/install?repo={{< var extension.wizard-reference >}}){.btn .btn-outline-primary title="Install {{< var extension.reference >}} in VSCodium using the Quarto Wizard extension."}

:::

::: {.callout-important}
Reference the filter by name, without an `at:` stage.
It registers itself at the several stages it needs, and pinning it to one breaks cross-referencing and the `math: typst` takeover.
:::

## Quick start

```yaml
filters:
  - typst-render
```

Then write Typst:

````markdown
```{typst}
#circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue)
```
````

Which compiles to this, as the page is built:

```{typst}
#circle(radius: 1cm, fill: blue)
```

Inline expressions work too, and scale to the surrounding text:

```markdown
A red word `{typst} #text(red)[hello]` in the middle of a sentence.
```

A red word `{typst} #text(red)[hello]` in the middle of a sentence.

See the [Reference](reference.qmd) for every option, and the [Examples](examples.qmd) for figures, tables, equations, and the options that shape them.

## Where it works

Every output format.
The Typst is compiled to an image, so HTML, PDF, Word, PowerPoint, and slides all receive the same figure.

Under Typst output the image is produced too, unless you ask for `output: asis`, which passes the code through natively instead.
